english_verification.review_scope: Checked current Mod names, opening history, subjects, and ideas; read the six specified English Wiki chunks for Cloud Giant foundation, Great Clan centralization, the 1440 Wiki accession date, and later historical context. The local 1438 country-history date remains separate. This is bounded source review, not an exhaustive mission-tree audit.
unresolved: The Wiki records Ziltagh's accession as 1440 while the current local country history records his monarch entry in 1438; the article preserves the conflict.
Wiki material after 1444 is historical context only and is not treated as an inevitable player outcome.
Mod and Wiki checks do not prove every mission branch or every article claim.

rationale.campaign_length: The structured database records 73 mission definitions, including mutually exclusive branches, hidden placeholders, and WIP Insyan segments.
rationale.colonization: Expansion is mainly through conquest and subjects, not colonization.
rationale.complexity: Religious reform, Hunger, subject loyalty, and dynamic mission branches must be managed together.
rationale.dark_story: Slave markets, forced labor, and destruction of cities are explicit dark elements.
rationale.difficulty: Religious pacing, war targets, subject relations, and construction gates create risks; not tested hands-on.
rationale.diplomacy: Vassals, tributaries, special subjects, and collaboration routes are central.
rationale.early_pressure: Recovery after the Centaur invasion, Doom, and clan relations create opening pressure.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: The Feast of the Gods, Giant heritage, and mage cooperation recur; war and subjects remain central.
rationale.narrative_density: Ziltagh, the Great Clans, goblins, Giant heirs, and multi-region rule form one story.
rationale.tall_play: The capital, Kelaktar, heartland, mage tower, and industry impose gates.
rationale.trade_economy: Merchant routes, agriculture, and a late treasure fleet support the economy; trade is not primary.
rationale.warfare: Subduing clans, expanding through the Ogre Valley and steppes, and contesting Giant heritage require war.

identity.appearance: A Fathide Ogre kingdom holding four provinces in 1444, with three vassals and three tributaries.
identity.formation_scope: Native in 1444; the dedicated tree is centered on I90 and has no mandatory tag change.

national_ideas.scope_note: National traditions, seven national ideas, and ambition only; excludes optional idea groups and racial or government bonuses. Conditional sets are listed separately and are not simultaneous.

description.text: Maghargma is the dominant power of the Ogres, ruling over a vast expanse of land and commanding the loyalty of all that tread its grounds. Though we may have forsaken our royal duties for centuries, we shall neglect the realm no more.
description.text_en: Maghargma is the dominant power of the Ogres, ruling over a vast expanse of land and commanding the loyalty of all that tread its grounds. Though we may have forsaken our royal duties for centuries, we shall neglect the realm no more.

description.text: Fighting for the glory of all Ogres and under the command of the warlords, our warriors fight without concern for their own well-being, comforted by the fact that their death shall feed and empower their fellow Ogre and that they died in honor of the realm.
description.text_en: Fighting for the glory of all Ogres and under the command of the warlords, our warriors fight without concern for their own well-being, comforted by the fact that their death shall feed and empower their fellow Ogre and that they died in honor of the realm.

description.text: The stagnation and decadence that gripped our realm for centuries was finally extinguished by the great King Ziltagh Gravelhide, who rallied the warlords to repel the Centaur menace and restored the pride and might of Maghargma. He instituted several reforms to ensure our warriors would never become indolent knaves, and so our rulers never fall into a pit of hedonism again.

description.text: We will not abide any disobedience among our own people, much less the weaklings we conquer. Our subjects know that any thoughts of rebellion will be ruthlessly quashed and those that continue to advocate for their "independence" shall be placed upon our dishes so we may inherit their boldness.

description.text: An Ogre's favorite weapon is a club, easy to create and use, and fully capable of shattering those that get in their way. Even while we move to using guns and cannons, we can still use our new weapons in the style we've used for eons, bludgeoning our enemies into bloody pulps when firepower cannot.

Even while we move to using guns and cannons, we can still use our new weapons in the style we've used for eons, bludgeoning our enemies into bloody pulps when firepower cannot.

description.text: Magic has quite a strange effect on Ogres, those that use it gain an insatiable hunger for damestear, the constant consumption of which causes them to undergo a kind of transformation, their skin turns blue, their builds become emaciated, and they adopt a more devious and cunning personality. While these traits may alarm many of our people, their ability on the battlefield ensures they will always find a place within our armies.

description.text: Owing to our large size, we can wield weaponry far outscaling those of the tiny humans, elves, or dwarves. While their rifles are but toothpicks for us, even our pistols would be counted as a cannon compared to their sizes, not to mention our muskets.

player_overview.avoid_if: Players who dislike subject loyalty, reforms, construction requirements, or who expect to play through all 73 defined missions in a single campaign.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Control Hunger, complete reform, consolidate Ziltagh, manage special subjects, expand through the steppes, then build the heartland and pursue Giant relics.
player_overview.overview: Maghargma begins in 1444 with four provinces, three vassals, and three tributaries. Reform the Feast of the Gods, manage Hunger and clans, choose direct occupation or special subjects, expand into the Centaur steppes, and pursue Giant heritage. The Insyan expedition still has placeholders.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy Ogre epics, religious pressure, subject networks, branching governance, and long imperial campaigns.
signature_features: Feast of the Gods reforms and Hunger pressure determine the pace of war and early missions.
Special subject territories do not use diplomatic slots; borderlands and the heartland can follow dynamic occupation or collaboration routes.
Move from the Ogre Valley into the Centaur steppes, Serpent Vale, and Giant sites while progressively claiming Giant succession.
player_overview.tagline: Rebuild an Ogre kingdom on Giant ruins and absorb the steppes through reform and subjects.

reasons: A rare Ogre royal epic built around a fallen Giant site
The Feast of the Gods and special subjects change the normal conquest rhythm
Multi-region dynamic routes make occupation and collaboration meaningful choices
warnings: Reform and Hunger can interrupt mission pacing
Subject loyalty and construction gates require management
The Insyan expedition nodes remain WIP prompts

phase_scores.phase: Cooperative governance and Troll alliance route
Troll husbandry and forced extraction route

positive_indicators: The goblin refugee event increases coexistence tolerance and establishes a Kelaktar
The western borderlands can sponsor a human special subject and increase human tolerance
Agricultural heartland, capital, and subject construction provide public output
values.rationale: War, Ogre species, and monarchy are not penalized by themselves. The opening event makes goblin clans royal property, while mission text involves slave markets, forced labor, and treating Centaurs as labor resources; the western occupation branch removes urban development, and the optional Troll-husbandry route treats sapient beings as renewable meat. Goblin city-states, local human cooperation, and a Troll alliance are mitigating routes, so the overall negative assessment is branch-dependent.
red_flags: The opening event makes goblin clans royal property, and mission text involves slave markets and forced labor
The western borderland occupation branch removes infrastructure and urban development
The optional Troll-husbandry route treats sapient beings as renewable meat
